Subject - Applicability of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (RFCTLARR) Act, 2013 in land acquisition under the National Highways (NH) Act, 1956.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Sir, I am directed to say that the Hon'ble High Court of Allahabad in the WP(C) No.13489 of 2024 titled as Shri Rampal Singh and 12 ors.

Vs.
National Highway Authority of India and 2 others has, inter alia, passed following order on 24.04.2024:

"Before parting, we may note that large numbers of cases are coming up before this court everyday complaining that rehabilitation and resettlement awards are not being made by the Competent Authority where acquisition is under the provisions of NH Act.

As the judgement of Division Bench of this Court in Ranvir Singh (Supra) is not challenge on merits, it is desirable that Central Government clarifies the legal position by issuing a circular so as to obviate filing of separate petitions by affected persons for direction to pass such an award."

2. In compliance of the above said order of the Hon'ble High Court, it is informed that the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has already clarified applicability of the RFCTLARR Act, 2013 in land acquisition under the National Highways Act, 1956 vide letter No. NH- 11011/30/2015-LA dated 28.12.2017 (copy enclosed)
3.

entities.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The comprehensive guidelines dated 28.12.2017 may please be brought into the notice of all concerned authorities dealing with acquisition of land and compensation therefor under the National Highways Act, 1956 for strict compliance.
Yours Sincerely, (Sanjay Kumar) Under Secretary to the Government of India 011-23719850."
4. Firstly, we note that while quoting our order dated 24.04.2024, there are typographical errors.

Shri S.P. Singh, learned Additional Solicitor General fairly admits the said fact and submits that a fresh circular would be issued wherein all caution would be taken not to repeat the mistake.
5.

We also drew attention of Shri S.P. Singh, learned Additional Solicitor General to the fact that the circular, though, intended to clarify the legal position, has been issued in a casual manner without actually clarifying the legal position.

Insofar as it refers to a previous circular dated 28.12.2017, we find that therein also while issuing directions in paragraph no.4.6 (iii), it is not specifically stated that provisions of Second Schedule relating to rehabilitation and resettlement compensation would apply to acquisitions made under National Highways Act.
It only speaks of compliances to be made under the First Schedule, which is regarding determination of compensation for the land acquired.

6. Shri S.P. Singh, learned Additional Solicitor General assures the Court that all care would be taken while issuing fresh circular and the concern of the Court regarding vagueness in the earlier circular, would be taken care of.

7. Having regard to the said statement, we dispose of the instant petition with liberty to the respondents to issue the required circular within three weeks and the same be communicated to this Court through the Registrar General and it will be placed on record of the instant case.
8.

In respect of the request of the petitioner for payment of rehabilitation and resettlement compensation, in view of admitted legal position that the acquisitions under National Highways Act would also be governed by Section 31 of the Act, 2013, we permit the petitioner to make representation before the competent authority alongwith true attested copy of the instant order for being granted benefits, as contemplated under the Second Schedule within two weeks from today.

On such representation being made, the competent authority will examine the claim of the petitioner and will pass appropriate order/award, as per the entitlement of the petitioner within next twelve weeks.
(Kshitij Shailendra, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
